subject: Alternative for multinomial and ordinal exogenous variables

messages.author: 5d6841cd822d7a3a
messages.subject: Alternative for multinomial and ordinal exogenous variables
parts:
Respected sir,
Am doing my masters in Biostatistics, India. Am doing my project related to path analysis. According to my knowledge, we need to create dummy variables if multinomial and ordinal exogenous variables are there in the model. Actually my moto of doing path analysis is whether the variable is having any direct or indirect effect to outcome variable not the categories of variable (For eg: wealth index (poor, middle and rich) which is exogenous variable in my path model to predict the educational level of children (no education, primary, secondary, higher). For the above stated example, I consider the outcome as ordinal and "lavaan" uses "probit ordinal regression model". For exogenous variable (wealth index), we need to create dummy variables. So, finally end up with two path coefficients for two dummy variables. Instead of using dummy variable, is there any other method to deal the exogenous variable which is having more than two categories? My direct question is, Can I get one path coefficient for above stated simple example? please help me in this regard.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Alternative for multinomial and ordinal exogenous variables
parts: Instead of using dummy variable, is there any other method to deal the exogenous variable which is having more than two categories? My direct question is, Can I get one path coefficient for above stated simple example?

What coefficient do you want to interpret?  Would you like to assume that the difference in latent education level (i.e., the normally distributed variable assumed to underlie the outcome's ordinal categories) is the same between "poor" and "middle" wealth as it is between "middle" and "rich" wealth?  To model a single linear effect under such an assumption, merely code the categories with equidistant numbers like (0, 1, 2) or (1, 2, 3), then enter that numeric variable as the predictor of education level.

But you can test whether that assumption is tenable by treating "middle" as the reference category (i.e., using dummy codes for "poor" and "rich" as the 2 predictors of education level).  You can label their slopes (which are both mean differences compared to "middle"), then define a parameter that is the difference between those slopes.  The summary() output will give you a z test of the null hypothesis that those mean differences are equal.  If it is significant, you can reject the null hypothesis of a single linear effect.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Respected sir,
I hereby attached the hypothesized path model of my study for your reference. My study is to find the direct and indirect effects for child marriage. I wish to find a single path coefficient which represent the effect of exogenous variable on endogenous variable . In my case, all variables except the child marriage (outcome which is binary) are ordinal variables.For that example I stated previously for wealth index of family and education of children, We hypothesized that poor income of family will lead to less education of children and as the income level increases from poor to other levels (middle or rich) , correspondingly their children's educational level also increases to the higher level. According to the theory of lavaan, if endogenous categorical variable which is having more than two categories, it can be treated as ordinal by declaring that variable are ordinal. If exogenous categorical variable which is having more than two categories, then need to create dummy variable. So, lavaan will predict the path coefficient by using ordinal probit regression model because of ordinal endogenous variable. As u answered above, if I find the path coefficient by the difference of slopes of two dummy variable, what will be the interpretation for above stated scenario?. If I consider the exogenous variable as continuous, what will be the issue over this?. Please help me in this regard sir.
Thank you very much for your response sir.
